{"id": "82d72417-e4e1-42b8-abac-452587b0f394", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "The error means EBS limits how many IOPS you can provision per GiB of volume size, and your request goes over that limit.

**The math**
- 20,000 IOPS ÷ 15 GiB = 1,333.3 IOPS per GiB.
- The limit for your volume is 1,000 IOPS per GiB, according to the error message.
- At 15 GiB, the most you can provision is 15 × 1,000 = **15,000 IOPS**.

**Ways to fix it**
1. **Raise IOPS to 15,000 or less.** This is the cheapest option.
2. **Grow the volume to at least 20 GiB, then request 20,000 IOPS.** 20 × 1,000 = 20,000, so that is exactly enough. You can change size and IOPS in the same `ModifyVolume` call. Volume size can only go up, never down, so this is a one-way change.

**Caveats**
- The 1,000 IOPS per GiB ratio is what your error reports, and it applies to io2 Block Express volumes. The documentation I found while checking still lists an older 500 IOPS per GiB ratio for io2 (that was the PGUIDE/ParallelCluster page). Treat the ratio in your error message as authoritative for your volume.
- Provisioned IOPS cost money every month, so check whether you need the full 20,000 before you resize.
- The full IOPS are only delivered on supported Nitro-based instance types. An instance that doesn't support them will cap your volume's performance regardless of what you provision.
- A volume can only be modified once every 6 hours, so settle on the right size and IOPS before you retry.

If you tell me the volume ID and region, I can check its current size, IOPS and attached instance type. Then you can pick the right target values.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
